title: Should social media be banned for children under 16?
description: The debate considers whether governments should prohibit social-media accounts for people younger than 16 to protect safety and wellbeing.

facts.fact: Australia's 2024 law requires certain social-media platforms to prevent children under 16 from holding accounts.
The Australian ban took effect on 10 December 2025 and covers platforms including Instagram, TikTok and Snapchat.
Platforms can be fined up to A$49.5 million for serious or repeated failures to prevent underage accounts.
The ban applies to account-based services, while gaming and messaging platforms are exempt.
Under-16s can still access some covered platforms, including YouTube, without creating an account.
The law depends on platforms building age-assurance systems, creating implementation and verification challenges.
